A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of the same survey. Their main text, Figure 1, references and Appendix A/Table 1 support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 synthesizes existing research and benchmarks. Its performance statements are attributed to cited work; neither the main text nor appendix reports original empirical results.

after.justification: V2 remains a literature survey. Added discussions and qualitative performance claims concern cited research, without original experiments, user studies or empirical data analyses.

M1.justification: Neither version proposes an implemented model or algorithm. V2 revises its account of MedFuzz and PDWS, but this concerns surveyed approaches rather than a method developed by the authors.

E1.justification: Neither version conducts training or evaluation on datasets. Appendix Table 1 retains the same 12 benchmarks and task descriptions; expanded multilingual coverage is proposed as future work.

E2.justification: Neither PDF evaluates a proposed system against baselines. Additional references and revised descriptions of existing approaches do not introduce evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: No experimental splits, metrics, model configurations, budgets or testing procedures are introduced or revised. Expanded calibration and abstention discussion explains surveyed practices.

E4.justification: No newly conducted ablations, robustness tests or supplementary empirical analyses appear. The expanded MedFuzz example and application trade-offs are literature synthesis and discussion.

E5.justification: Neither version reports original repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Calibration and uncertainty remain survey topics, with no changed statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: Quoted Med-PaLM accuracies of 67.6% and 86.5%, and the 60% ECE reduction, remain unchanged. Section 3 newly asserts that combining MedFuzz with PDWS-guided fine-tuning reduces degradation under perturbations; this is an added qualitative literature claim, not an original measurement.

T1.justification: No mathematical definitions, formal assumptions, theorems, proofs or derivations are added or revised. The new distinction between plausible and faithful explanations is conceptual.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: six trustworthiness dimensions, evaluation-guided improvement, benchmark synthesis and future research directions. Their scientific scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 adds qualifications distinguishing clinical demographic differences from unfair bias and explanation plausibility from faithfulness. It expands application-specific trade-offs and English-language limitations, recasts the MedFuzz–PDWS relationship, and relabels Table 1's reasoning benchmarks as explainability benchmarks.

D1.justification: Limitations newly identifies searched venue families, arXiv inclusion and publication-year scope; v1 only specifies topical exclusions. These disclose aspects of the review process without establishing a changed experimental procedure.

R1.justification: V2 adds supporting works by Agarwal, Jones, Guo, Lewis and Guu on faithfulness, medical dataset bias, calibration and retrieval. It also revises the relationship presented between MedFuzz and PDWS, while retaining the survey's overall research positioning.

P1.justification: The main section order remains intact. V2 locally rewrites robustness and calibration passages, expands Challenges and Limitations, adds Acknowledgements, and updates the author and affiliation block, including Baiyang Wang.

P2.justification: Figure 1 corrects all six misassigned dimension labels and garbled citations. Table 1 retains its rows and columns but changes Hallucination labels to Factuality and Reasoning labels to Explainability. Display structures remain essentially unchanged.

improvement.justification: Correcting Figure 1 removes a clear contradiction with Section 2, while the fairness and faithfulness qualifications improve conceptual precision. These provide a limited net gain. The unexplained PDWS redefinition and integration claim in Section 3, together with Table 1's unsupported reasoning-to-explainability reclassification, limit confidence in the expanded synthesis.
